ReactFlight > should error if useContext.note: Asserts that ReactServer.useContext doesn't exist in the react-server build. Stores are read with use(), which the server build has; the store error for a Server Component is covered by the use() cases in the copy.

ReactFlightDOM > does not throw when acc.note: Accessing .Provider on a client reference proxy to a context. Stores have no Provider.

ReactFlightDOM > can render a client Con.note: A Server Component provides the value that a client component reads. A Server Component can't read or set a store, and a store has no Provider to render, so there's no way for the server to choose the value per subtree.

ReactContextValidator > should pass next.note: A class with static contextType reads this.context and nextContext in its lifecycles. Stores can't be read from class components.

ReactContextValidator > should re-render.note: A PureComponent with static contextType re-renders when the Provider updates. Stores can't be read from class components; the function-component version of this propagation is covered by ReactContextPropagationUseStoreContext (memo HOC).

ReactContextValidator > should warn if b.note: Warning about a class defining both contextType and contextTypes.

ReactContextValidator > should warn if a.note: Warning about an invalid static contextType.

ReactContextValidator > should warn if y.note: Warning about contextType on a function component.

ReactElementValidator > gives a helpful.note: Uses createContext().Consumer as an example of a valid element type. A store isn't an element type.

ReactIs > identifies valid element types.note: Checks that Context.Provider and Context.Consumer are valid element types. A store isn't an element type, and react-is has no store type.

ReactIs > should identify elements.note: Checks that <Context.Provider> and <Context.Consumer> are elements. Stores aren't rendered as elements.

react-devtools-facade > getComponentTree.note: Asserts the Context.Provider node in the component tree. Stores have no Provider fiber.

InspectedElement > should have hasLegacy.note: Tests the inspector's legacy vs modern context flag for Consumer, contextType and legacy contextTypes readers. A store read isn't context, and it shows up as a hook (covered by the 'only use context' copies).

InspectedElement > should properly handl.note: The only context read is DevTools' own TreeDispatcherContext/TreeStateContext, used to drive the frontend.
